title: Libby trial-screener row
description: One row per publication (per the trial-table style). Appended to data/cases/<slug>/trials.jsonl by trial_screener.

row_id.description: Stable ID for the trial-publication row (slug-PMID or NCT).

toxicity_flags.description: Toxicity-veto fragments from preferences.json that this regimen triggers.

tumor_type_relationship.description: How does this trial relate to the patient's tumor type? `primary_indication_match` = trial enrolls the patient's tumor type. `basket_or_biomarker_match` = trial accepts the patient based on biomarker regardless of tumor type — most under-recognized actionable opportunity for rare-disease patients. `same_drug_other_indication` = drug proven elsewhere being tested in the patient's tumor type. `cross_tumor_extrapolation` = trial is in a different tumor type but informs the evidence base; not directly enrollable for this patient. Default (omitted) = primary_indication_match.

aliases.description: Every known identifier for the intervention drug — generic INN/USAN, pharma code(s), dev-program code, nicknames. e.g. ['gocatamig', 'MK-6070', 'HPN328', 'DS3280']. The screener uses this to detect duplicate registry hits and to keep its alias-expansion search complete. Always include the agent's primary name in the list for round-tripping.

modality.description: Therapeutic modality. Drives the modality cross-product search in trial_screener Step 1.5. The screener must enumerate the full <feature> × <modality> grid before declaring discovery complete.

development_status.description: Development status as of the most recent registry / publication signal. `discontinued` and `legacy_research_only` rows are kept (informational) so the board sees the full mechanism evidence base — not just active programs. Failed-but-instructive entries (e.g. Rova-T post-TAHOE) are decision-relevant context.

regulatory_status.description: Regulatory-approval status of the trial's intervention WITH RESPECT TO THE PATIENT'S INDICATION. `investigational` = pre-approval for any indication. `approved_off_label` = drug has FDA / EMA / equivalent approval for some indication other than the patient's (the drug can be prescribed off-label even if the trial doesn't fit). `approved_on_label` = drug is approved for the patient's indication (rare in pipeline-context rows by definition — pipeline-context exists for *cross-tumor* trials the patient cannot enroll in). `withdrawn` = previously approved, now withdrawn or revoked. Drives the off-label pill on the pipeline-context table: rows tagged `approved_off_label` (or `approved_on_label` when the trial's enrolling indication is cross-tumor) render an `off-label` flag so the reader sees that the drug exists in the market and could in principle be prescribed off-label, even though this specific trial isn't a match.

sponsor.description: Corporate or academic developer (Boehringer Ingelheim, Merck, Harpoon→Merck, Amgen, Innovent, Daiichi/AbbVie, Memorial Sloan Kettering, etc.). Useful for the user to assess feasibility of access and to follow news flow.
